question: In group 2 of the Modern Periodic Table, the valency of elements is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Group 2 of the Modern Periodic Table, elements are known as** alkaline earth metals.**
 
• These elements have **two valence electrons** in their outermost shell.
 
• Which they lose during chemical reactions when achieving a stable electron configuration.
 
• Here is the list of Group 2 elements: **Beryllium(Be), Magnesium(Mg), Calcium(Ca), Strontium(Sr), Barium(Ba), Radium (Ra)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev**, a Russian chemist, is credited with creating the** first version of the periodic table in 1869.**
 
• The **Modern Periodic Law **states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.
 
• The periodic table currently has **118 elements**. Elements with atomic numbers 1 to 94 occur naturally, while elements 95 to 118 are synthetic and created in laboratories.
 
• There are **18 groups** (vertical columns) and **7 periods** (horizontal rows) in the table.
 
• Hydrogen (H) and Helium (He) are the **most abundant elements** in the universe. Hydrogen makes up about 75% of the universe's elemental mass.
 
• Uranium (U), with atomic number 92, is the** heaviest naturally occurring element**.
 
• Elements with atomic numbers greater than 104 are known as **superheavy elements**. They are highly unstable and exist for only fractions of a second after creation in laboratories.
